Any person who would like to address the Legislative Bodies on any agendized item is requested to complete a speaker card for the City Clerk/Agency/Authority Secretary and identify the agenda item you would like to discuss. At each regular City Council Meeting, the City Council is presented with the financial claims (invoices) against the City for purchase of materials, supplies, services, and capital projects for checks and Automated Clearing House (ACH) payments issued the prior two to three weeks. This process provides the City Council the opportunity to review the expenses of the City. The justifying backup information for each expenditure is available in the Finance Department.

CC 4. Adopt Resolution No. 18-16, authorizing the City Manager, or his designee, to apply for $5,482,120 of funds available to the City of Lancaster from Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority (LACMTA).
Annually, Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority allocates Transportation Development Act (TDA) Article 8 funds to fund unmet transit needs in areas outside the Metro service area. Article 8 revenues will be used by the City to fund Council-approved and budgeted Capital Improvement Projects and operating transfers.

CC 5. Approve the Sub-Recipient Agreement between the City of Lancaster and the Housing Rights Center to provide fair housing services to the residents of Lancaster for the 2018 Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Program Year.
The City has engaged the Housing Rights Center to provide the fair housing services in the 2016 2017 CDBG Program Year and in prior years. A letter was received from the Executive Director of the Housing Rights Center, dated May 4, 2018, stating their desire to continue to provide fair housing services to the City of Lancaster. In compliance with Federal Regulations Title 24, Part 570, Section 570.503, HUD requires that the City of Lancaster (the â€œRecipientâ€) enter into a written agreement with the Housing Rights Center (the â€œSub-Recipientâ€) in order for the City to grant its entitlement funds to the sub-recipient for providing fair housing services.

CC 6. Accept the work constructed by Granite Construction Company for Public Works Construction Project No. 16-009, 2016 Pavement Management Program; and direct the City Clerk to file the Notice of Completion for the project. Retention on this project has been disbursed in accordance with California Public Contract Code.
On May 9, 2017, Council awarded Public Works Construction Project No. 16-009, 2016 Pavement Management Program to Granite Construction Company. The streets that were resurfaced include 20th Street East (Avenue K-8 to Avenue L), 20th Street East (Avenue J to Avenue K), East Avenue J-8 (Rodin Avenue to Challenger Way), East Avenue J-8 (Challenger Way to 20th Street East), East Avenue J-8 (20th Street East to 22nd Street East), East Avenue K (Division Street to Challenger Way), 40th Street West (Avenue K to Avenue L), and Avenue L (52nd Street West to 55th Street West). To provide connectivity and improve safety, in accordance with the Master Plan of Trails and Bikeways and Master Plan of Complete Streets, streets were re-striped and new bike lanes were installed.

CC 6 attachment
CC 7. Approve Professional Service Agreements with the pre-qualified consulting firms: Interwest Consulting Group, Bureau Veritas/California Code Check, and JAS Pacific; and authorize the City Manager, or his designee, to execute all task orders within existing signature authority limits.
On March 22, 2018, the City advertised Request for Qualifications (RFQ) No. 679-18 for Building and Safety Plan Review and Inspection Services. Eight (8) proposals were received by the submission deadline on April 17, 2018. An evaluation committee from Development Services evaluated the proposals based on evaluation criteria identified in the RFQ. These criteria were: demonstrated successful experience with similar types of projects, specific experience of key project team members, satisfaction of previous clients (references), project understanding and approach, cost of service, and proposed on multiple tasks. Based on the evaluation criteria, Interwest Consulting Group, Bureau Veritas/California Code Check, and JAS Pacific received the highest overall scores for all tasks.

CC 8. Determine the need for creation of easement by covenant, allowing ingress and egress over properties held in common ownership for the benefit of future owners; and authorize the City Clerk to endorse and record at the County of Los Angeles Recorders Office this Covenant of Easement.
Due to improvements being constructed by Public Works Construction Project 17-020 the â€œAvenue I Corridor Improvementsâ€, some portions of access to Avenue I will be shifted or removed completely. Monte Vista Company, a California Corporation, is the owner of two distinct and adjoining parcels of real property located at 1110 West Avenue I and 1114 West Avenue I, in the City of Lancaster. The closing of the driveway at 1114 West Avenue I necessitates a covenant of easement to allow ingress and egress to parking areas of 1114 West Avenue I through the driveway located at 1110 West Avenue I.

CC 9. Authorize the City Manager to make progress payments up to $1,100,000.00 to Viper Enterprises pursuant to the Reimbursement Agreement dated March 14, 2017.
On March 12, 2017, the City Council approved a Reimbursement Agreement with Viper Enterprises to facilitate development of a new dealership in the Lancaster Auto Mall, and installation of high-quality improvements to the public realm. The dealership is currently under construction and is anticipated to open before the end of the year. The proposed authorization would allow the City of Lancaster to satisfy its commitment to Viper Enterprises, while securing the completion of the public improvements.

CC 10. Renewed Downtown Lancaster Property-Based Improvement District (PBID)
CC 10
CC 10 attachment
a.
Adopt Resolution No. 18-17 initiating proceedings and declaring intent to renew the Downtown Lancaster Property and Business Improvement District.
b.
Set a Public Hearing for July 24, 2018 to consider renewal of the PBID.
The initial five-year term of the Lancaster Property and Business Improvement District (the â€œDistrictâ€) is drawing to a close. Applicable law (the Property and Business Improvement District Law of 1994, Cal. Sts. & High. Code Â§ 36600 et seq. (the â€œPBID Lawâ€)) provides that the District may be renewed by following the procedures for establishing a new district and that, upon renewal, the District shall have a term of not more than ten years. (See Cal. Sts. & High. Code Â§ 36660(a), (c).)
The City has received written petitions signed by the property or business owners in the District who will pay more than fifty percent (50%) of the assessments proposed to be levied requesting that proceedings be initiated to renew the District. Therefore, the City Council may now adopt a resolution initiating proceedings and declaring its intent to renew the District, which begins the renewal process.
The Resolution now before you for consideration does the following: (a) finds that the City has received written petitions signed by the property or business owners in the District who will pay more than fifty percent (50%) of the assessments proposed to be levied; (b) initiates proceedings and declares the City Councilâ€™s intent to renew the District; (c) sets forth a brief description of the proposed improvements, maintenance, and activities, the amount of the proposed assessment, a statement as to whether the assessment will be levied on property or businesses within the district, a statement as to whether bonds will be issued, and a description of the exterior boundaries of the proposed district; and (d) sets a time and place for a public hearing on the Districtâ€™s renewal and the levy of assessments.

Award the design contract to Stantec Consulting Services, Inc., of Lancaster, California, for Task Order No. 26, in accordance with the 2016-2018 Multi-Year Professional Services Agreement, in the amount of $164,852.00 with a 10% contingency; and authorize the City Manager, or his designee, to sign all documents.
The proposed project will â€œright-sizeâ€ the travel way on 10th Street West between Avenue H and Lancaster Boulevard, to allow for enhancement of streetscape within the existing right-of-way. ADA accessibility will be addressed throughout; intersections will be upgraded to include pedestrian refuge areas/islands, crossings will be shortened, and upraised hand timers will be replaced with countdown timers.

Lancaster Landscape Maintenance District No. 1 and Fox Field Industrial Corridor Landscape Maintenance District were formed, including subsequent annexations thereto, for the purpose of providing maintenance services to landscaping and appurtenant improvements for various developments within the City, and assessing those properties which benefit from this service. The City Council previously formed the Lancaster Drainage Benefit Assessment District, including establishment of separate zones, and submitted the proposition to the eligible voters in each respective zone. The majority of voters approved the formation of the District, the separate zones, and the levying of the assessment. The first year's assessment was paid by the developers of the property. Each year, thereafter, the City Council, after public notice and hearing, may determine and impose an annual assessment.

Adopt Resolution No. 18-24, a resolution of the City Council of the City of Lancaster, California, levying Lancaster Sewer System Service Charges for maintenance and servicing of the Lancaster Sewer System, for Fiscal Year 2018-2019.
Each year, staff prepares an Engineer's Report for the City Council to determine the actual amount of the sewer service charge needed to fund the maintenance of the Lancaster Sewer System. NB 1. Award Public Works Construction Project No. 18-006, 2018 Sidewalk, Curb and Gutter Repairs, to Hardy & Harper, Inc., of Santa Ana, California
Recommendation:
Award Public Works Construction Project No. 18-006, 2018 Sidewalk, Curb and Gutter Repairs, to Hardy & Harper, Inc., of Santa Ana, California, in the amount of $1,976,000.00, plus a 10% contingency, for curb and gutter, sidewalk, and pedestrian curb ramp replacement, as well as tree removal/root pruning; and authorize the City Manager, or his designee, to sign all documents. This contract is awarded to the lowest responsible bidder per California Public Code Section 22038 (b).
Under the Summer of Sidewalks program, the 2018 Sidewalk, Curb and Gutter Repair project will be repairing or replacing 78,000 SF of sidewalk, 3,671 linear feet (LF) of curb and gutter, and 5,193 SF of cross gutters and spandrels. The project includes the root pruning and tree trimming of over 260 trees. This will help reduce the need to remove mature trees at the various repair locations, while helping prevent future trip hazards, normally caused by overgrown tree roots. In addition, the City will improve 192 curb ramps in compliance with the City of Lancasterâ€™s 2014 ADA Transition Plan.

NB 2. Presentation on Process to Adjust Transient Occupancy Tax Rate
Recommendation:
Review and file a report on the process to undertake to increase the Transit Occupancy Tax (TOT) rate.
The City of Lancasterâ€™s TOT was established in 1983 and is currently assessed at 7%. In addition, there is a self-imposed 2% fee collected for the Lancaster Tourism Business Improvement District (Destination Lancaster). These funds are managed and distributed by Destination Lancaster for the benefit of the members.
NB 2
NB 3. Extension and Modifications to the First Amendment to Amended and Restated Agreement for the Collection of Solid Waste effective December 14, 2012 and Amended and Restated Agreement for the Collection of Solid Waste effective May 22, 2007 between the City of Lancaster and Waste Management of Antelope Valley
Recommendation:
Authorize the City Manager and City Attorney to prepare and execute an extension and modifications to the First Amendment to Amended and Restated Agreement for the Collection of Solid Waste effective December 14, 2012 (â€œAmendmentâ€) and Amended and Restated Agreement for the Collection of Solid Waste effective May 22, 2007 (â€œRestated Agreementâ€) between the City of Lancaster and Waste Management (WM) of Antelope Valley as specified in this staff report; and authorize the City Manager, or his designee, to sign all documents.
The City of Lancaster has granted to Waste Management Inc. (WMI) a franchise for the collection and disposal of solid waste and recyclable materials since 1991. In April 2007, the City Council authorized modifications to the franchise agreement to update the contract language and overall service requirements, which resulted in the May 22, 2007 Restated Agreement. This was necessitated by numerous changes to state law, regulations, and case law, as well as a desire to modify rate escalators and related fees, the term of the agreement, and overall service levels.
For the last several months, representatives from the City and Waste Management have been in discussions regarding a potential contract extension to the Agreement along with a simplified, predictable, and negotiated Consumer Price Index (CPI) rate adjustment to replace the more complex and volatile rate adjustment methodologies currently included in the Amendment. Based on these discussions, the City and Waste Management representatives have agreed on tentative modifications to the Restated Agreement and Amendment, as detailed below, to recommend for approval by the City Council. Staff believes that the proposed Second Amendment would be of real benefit to the residents and businesses of the City of Lancaster in terms of rate stability and predictability, along with additional one-time revenue to support City Council authorized programs, services, and initiatives through the FY 2018-2019 and subsequent City budgets.
